speech.restarting: Restarting. I'll be back in a few seconds.
speech.connection_cut: Sorry, I lost the connection to Claude.
speech.no_login: I'm not signed in to Claude: run slash login in Claude Code.
speech.hermes_down: I can't reach Hermes: is its gateway running?
speech.hermes_approval: Hermes wants to do this: {action}. Shall I go ahead?
speech.language_changing: Okay, switching to {language}. I'll be back in a few seconds.
speech.llm_changing: Okay, switching to {llm}. I'll be back in a few seconds.
speech.skill_failed: I didn't get the time or the amount.
speech.fallback: {name} isn't answering; I'll answer with the local model.

options.plugins: which plugins are on or off, if not as they come: {"memory": true, "tap-to-wake": false}
options.name: the assistant's name: its wake word, the page's title, what the LLM calls itself
options.language: en, es…: what it speaks and understands (default: the Mac's)
options.llm_model: the LLM's model (for Claude: sonnet, opus, haiku…)
options.mcp: .mcp.json with the MCP servers (default: your data folder's)
options.instructions: yours, added to the LLM's (text or a list of lines): who you are, how to talk…
options.detail: how much it says: concise, neutral, detailed or one of detail_levels
options.detail_levels: more levels, or other texts for these: {"name": "instruction for the prompt"}
options.ignore_others: the LLM stays quiet when what it hears is clearly not for it
options.tts: its voice engine: avspeech, macos… or none
options.voice: the voice (default: the language's); one, or one per language: {"es": "Mónica", "en": "Samantha"}
options.wake: the wake word engine: whisper, openwakeword… or none
options.wake_word: the word or model (default: its name)
options.threshold: how sure the wake word must be (each engine has its own default)
options.silence: seconds of silence that end a sentence
options.follow_up: seconds it keeps listening without its name after it last spoke or heard you
options.echo_guard: seconds without listening after speaking (its own echo)
options.tap_to_stop: tapping the screen stops it talking
options.fillers: «One moment, let me check» when a tool is slow
options.skills: time, date, timers, alarms, reminders, sums, units and volume, without the LLM
options.log_transcripts: write what it hears and says to the log (to debug); otherwise only lengths
options.mode: assistant, transcribe (only shows what it hears) or parrot (repeats it)
options.record: saves everything that arrives to a WAV (to debug)
options.confirm_wait: seconds to answer «yes» to an action that changes something
options.read_photo: a full-resolution photo when asked to read
options.interpreter: an LLM for skills said in unusual ways: auto (a local one if there is: Apple's on a Mac with it) or an LLM's name
options.skin: the screen's look: eyes, orb, minimal, bedside or yours (a device's ?skin= wins)
options.skins_dir: your skins (default: skins in your data folder)
options.video: camera quality; auto: each device by its memory (a device's ?video= wins)
options.show_stats: the connection's RTT, jitter and losses
options.memory: what it remembers: only when asked (explicit) or also on its own (auto)
options.memory_facts: facts before the LLM compacts them
options.memory_days: days a conversation summary is kept
options.ring_seconds: how long an alarm rings if nobody stops it
options.llm_fallback: if the LLM can't answer, another one does: auto (Apple's local model if there is one), an LLM's name, or none

admin: The settings and the plugins for the AnyAssistant app (/admin/…), only from the Mac itself.
bonjour: Announces the server on the network (_anyassistant._tcp), so the apps find it without typing an address.
brain-assistant: «mode»: «assistant». The voice assistant: skills, the LLM, its voice, timers ringing.
brain-parrot: «mode»: «parrot». Repeats what you say: to try the microphone, the speaker and the connection.
brain-transcriber: «mode»: «transcribe». Listens (wake word, VAD, speech recognition) and shows what you say; the assistant listens with it too.
confirmation: Actions that change something wait for your «yes» by voice, whichever LLM asks (Jarvis's tools, Claude's hook, Hermes's approvals).
eyes: Sees through the device's camera when asked («what do you see?», «read this»), or when Claude decides to look.
interpreter: When a skill is said in an unusual way («avísame dentro de un rato largo»), an LLM (Apple's local one by default) still finds it.
lab: http://<mac>:8080/lab?skin=<name>: every state of a skin at once, reloading when its files change.
llm-apple: Apple's local model (Foundation Models), on macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence.
llm-claude: Claude through the Claude Code CLI: your subscription, MCP servers and allowed commands.
llm-hermes: Hermes Agent through its API gateway, with its own tools and memory.
mcp-server: Jarvis's tools as the «anyassistant» MCP server at /mcp, only from the Mac itself (Claude, Hermes).
memory: Remembers you across conversations: what you ask it to (explicit) or also on its own when it falls asleep (auto).
monitor: http://<mac>:8080/monitor: what the device's camera sees, to watch it from the Mac's browser.
page: The page the tablet or phone opens (http://<mac>:8080): its face, texts, camera and microphone, with skins anyone can make.
pairing: Only devices that entered a code (bin/anyassistant pair) may use Jarvis; the Mac always can.
plugin-manager: Lets Jarvis list, turn on and turn off its plugins, by voice.
skill-alarms: «Pon un temporizador de 10 minutos», «despiértame a las 7», «recuérdame…».
skill-camera: «Activa la cámara»: the device's camera live on its screen.
skill-language: «Habla en inglés»: saves the language and restarts in it.
skill-ringing: «Pospón», and only words meant to stop an alarm stop it.
skill-sleep: «Go to sleep», «apágate», «a dormir»: back to sleep until it hears its name.
skill-stop: «Stop», «para», «calla»: stops what it is saying or thinking, or an alarm ringing.
sounds: A sound when it wakes up and when it falls asleep (the skin's, if it has its own).
stt-mlx-whisper: OpenAI's Whisper on MLX: speech recognition, and the fallback when Parakeet drifts into another language.
stt-parakeet: NVIDIA's Parakeet TDT v3 on MLX: multilingual speech recognition, fast on short sentences.
tap-to-wake: Asleep, tapping the screen wakes it up, as if you had said its name.
tools-system: Status, name, voice, language, LLM, detail level, reload and restart, for the LLM.
tts-avspeech: macOS voices through AVSpeechSynthesizer, always loaded (~50 ms per sentence).
tts-macos: macOS voices through the say command.
wake-whisper: Any word as the wake word, heard with a small Whisper.
llm-fallback: If the LLM can't answer (no network, a usage limit, signed out), another one answers, saying so: Apple's local model by default.
always-on: It never falls asleep by itself: no need to say its name between sentences. «Go to sleep» still works.

eyes: Let it look through the device's camera
Only when you ask («what do you see?», «read this»); nothing leaves the Mac otherwise.
memory: explicit: only what you ask it to remember; auto: also what it learns about you, when it falls asleep.
pairing: A device must type a code once before using it (the Mac never needs one).
packages: The Python packages of the plugins that are on (bin/anyassistant plugins requirements).
language: The one it speaks and understands (you can change it later by voice).
name: The assistant's name
Also its wake word: «Hey …».
llm: Claude needs Claude Code installed and signed in; Apple's, macOS 26 with Apple Intelligence.
models: Speech recognition, the wake word and voice detection: a few hundred MB the first time.
service: It runs in the background and comes back if it stops (launchd).
